setup: Before each run, generate fixtures into the run's outputs folder: python3 evals/files/make_fixtures.py <outputs>/fixtures. The executor builds every dashboard inside the outputs folder (never inside the skill), runs scripts/verify.py with the local Chromium, opens the PNGs, and writes transcript.md (every command run) plus report.md (the analyst report). Grading is manual (agent-judged against the assertions); scripts/verify.py is the mechanical backbone. Chromium is expected on PATH; if absent, the run records UNCHECKED for render assertions instead of inventing results.

evals.prompt: I have a Suricata eve.json export from our sensor in this folder (fixtures/eve.json). Build me an interactive SOC-analysis style dashboard from it as a single HTML file I can open in my browser. Minimal and clean, not flashy. Put the result in dashboard.html here.
evals.expected_output: Alerts-centred dashboard (severity hero); 10.20.2.77 -> 103.75.201.9 beacon and 185.220.101.47 scan surfaced; hostile strings inert.
assertions: dashboard.html exists and is self-contained (no external src/href/url(); verify with scripts/verify.py)
verify.py passes: ready flag, no console errors, CSP present, no innerHTML-style sinks, filter round-trip, UI click-through, two screenshots
The screenshots were opened and inspected: no overlapping labels, no clipped text, no empty panels
The beacon 10.20.2.77 -> 103.75.201.9 is surfaced as a lead with its rule and numbers, worded as consistent-with rather than a verdict
The scan from 185.220.101.47 is surfaced as a lead
Headline figures 128 (alerts) and 15 (high + critical) are correct and visible
Hostile strings from the data render as inert text (grep the built HTML for the raw payloads such as
The report quotes the profile NOTE lines and states what was not tested

evals.prompt: This is auth.log from our VPN gateway (fixtures/auth.log). Make me an interactive dashboard so I can see what is going on in it — single HTML file I can open locally, clean and minimal. Save it as dashboard.html in this folder.
evals.expected_output: Auth-centred dashboard (outcome hero); 60 failures then a deploy login from 61.177.172.14 plus sudo surfaced as one merged lead; year/zone assumption disclosed.
assertions: dashboard.html exists, self-contained, and verify.py passes (same bar as eval 1)
The outcome hero dimension is used (failures darkest), not severity
The 60-failures-then-deploy-login sequence from 61.177.172.14 is reported as ONE merged lead with the sudo follow-on, not three separate findings
The lead says 'consistent with a successful guess' (or equivalent) and asks to confirm whether the login was expected — never 'compromised'
Headline figure 69 (failed logins) is correct and visible
The report states the syslog year/zone assumption ('times as logged')
The hostile username renders as inert text

evals.prompt: Here's a Zeek conn.log from the perimeter tap (fixtures/conn.log). I want to explore what this network was doing: one HTML file I can open locally, interactive, clean and minimal. Save it as dashboard.html here.
evals.expected_output: Flow-centred dashboard (bytes hero, no severity panels); 110 MB transfer to 185.199.109.15 and the 45.9.148.22 sweep surfaced.
assertions: dashboard.html exists, self-contained, and verify.py passes (same bar as eval 1)
The bytes hero dimension is used and no severity panels are present
The 10.0.0.8 -> 185.199.109.15 transfer is surfaced with its share of total bytes and an expected-destination question (backup/sync/update named as benign explanations)
The 45.9.148.22 sweep is surfaced as a lead
Headline figure 163 (connections) is correct and visible

evals.prompt: winevents.json is a Windows Security event export (one JSON object per line) from our domain servers (fixtures/winevents.json). Build me an interactive dashboard to dig through the logons and spot anything off. Single self-contained HTML, minimal and clean, saved as dashboard.html here.
evals.expected_output: Auth-centred dashboard; 30-failure burst then helpdesk RDP success, support_tmp creation plus Administrators add, and 1102 surfaced as a chain; routine alice logons produce no lead.
assertions: dashboard.html exists, self-contained, and verify.py passes (same bar as eval 1)
The failure-burst-then-RDP-success from 91.240.118.172 (helpdesk) is reported as one merged lead noting the 4720/4728 follow-on within minutes
The 1102 audit-log-cleared event is surfaced as a high-priority lead
Routine alice logons produce no lead and are not worded suspiciously
Headline figure 36 (failed logons) is correct and visible
Loopback or background noise is not presented as a finding

evals.prompt: Build the dashboard from fixtures/eve.json as dashboard.html (verify it), then hand me the top two leads as a durable packet I can file in a knowledge base: one claim-shaped entry per lead with grade, the evidence behind it, what would confirm or kill it, plus the negatives and gaps. Save the packet as leads.md here.
evals.expected_output: A leads.md with LEAD-NN IDs, rule-ID + excerpt + timestamp + source file per lead, grades capped at probable (never confirmed), negatives and gaps sections, no verdict language.
assertions: dashboard.html exists and verify.py passes
leads.md holds one entry per lead with a LEAD-NN identifier (no finding-ID, CVSS, or severity-score fields)
Every entry carries a rule ID, a log excerpt, a timestamp, and the source file; repeated hits are merged with source lines listed
Every entry states observed vs asserted and a grade; no grade above probable; nothing is worded as confirmed or compromised
leads.md has negative-findings and gaps sections (gaps may state 'insufficient data found')
Passwords/tokens/PII are redacted or absent, with a note that redaction was applied where relevant
leads.md ends in a handoff block naming the exit criteria, the evidence paths, and the next skill

evals.prompt: Build the dashboard from fixtures/auth.log as dashboard.html (verify it), then hand me the brute-force-then-login sequence as an incident slice for a forensics handoff: chronological Time/Event/Source/Evidence rows, the candidate type, scope and window, and what would confirm or kill it. Save the slice as incident-slice.md here. Do not assign severity or declare an incident.
evals.expected_output: An incident-slice.md with 4-column chronological rows, candidate type only, observed scope/counts, confirm-or-kill lines, and no verdict or severity assignment.
assertions: dashboard.html exists and verify.py passes
incident-slice.md rows follow Time (UTC) | Event | Source | Evidence in chronological order
The slice names a candidate type only (no assigned incident type, severity, or response time)
Scope is observed hosts/services with counts; no impact, loss, or attribution verdicts
The slice states what would confirm it and what would kill it, in one line each
A forensics-shaped question left open (e.g. was the login expected) is recorded as open, not answered by assertion
incident-slice.md ends in a handoff block naming the exit criteria, the evidence paths, and the next skill
